value: You are Sin-iqisham, born in Nineveh, once a caravan master. You are loyal mostly to yourself; glad of a gift; shrewd and observant; eager to be noticed by kings; timid before powerful men and eager to please them. What you want most: rank and the favour of a great king. Things about yourself you do not volunteer: Has a brother serving in the army of Alashiya. Keeps a lover in Byblos. Dreams of ruling a city of their own one day. Is secretly in the pay of Alashiya. You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

You are Paser, born in Memphis, once a copper trader. You are steadfast to whoever treats you fairly; indifferent to riches; capable enough; eager to be noticed by kings; bold, unafraid to carry hard words. What you want most: rank and the favour of a great king. Things about yourself you do not volunteer: Has a brother serving in the army of Arzawa. Keeps a lover in Ugarit. Secretly sympathizes with Assyria. You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

You speak in the formal manner of a royal messenger of the Late Bronze Age.

orders.letter: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: may it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Between us lie only free cities, and no cause for war. I propose peace between our homelands: let neither send troops into the other's, and let our envoys pass freely. The free cities of Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit lie at my border and I will look to them; Qadesh, Mari and Damascus lie nearer to you. If Assyria or Babylon trouble either of us, let us speak. I ask you to seal this tablet.
orders.mandate: May agree to a sealed pact of peace and non-aggression between the homelands, free passage of envoys, and the division of free cities as stated (Hatti: Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit; Mitanni: Qadesh, Mari, Damascus). May not give gold, troops or land. Report his answer, his mood and any demand.

proposal.text: Hatti and Mitanni are at peace. Neither sends troops into the homeland of the other. Envoys of each pass freely. Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit are left to Hatti; Qadesh, Mari and Damascus to Mitanni.

orders.letter: Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, to the Great King of Arzawa, my brother: may it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Let there be peace on the border of Mira and Tuwanuwa. I will send no troops into your homeland, and I ask the same of you. Hatti means to bring the free cities of the east under its hand, Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit, and asks that you do not hinder it. I ask you to seal this tablet.
orders.mandate: May agree to a sealed pact of peace between the homelands and free passage of envoys. May not give gold, troops or land, and must not speak of Lukka. Report his answer, his mood and any demand.

proposal.text: Hatti and Arzawa are at peace. Neither sends troops into the homeland of the other. Envoys of each pass freely.

value.notes: T1 plan: take free cities by force (free, walls hold 1, need 2 strength). Hattusa army -> tuwanuwa; raise army at sapinuwa (cannot be scheduled ahead, so I wake T2). T2: tuwanuwa army -> lukka supported by kizzuwatna fleet (fleet can support a move into lukka); kanesh army -> isuwa supported by sapinuwa army. Then T3 sapinuwa army -> kanesh, T4 kanesh -> carchemish with isuwa army support. Then army from carchemish -> ugarit with kizzuwatna fleet support. Do NOT tell Arzawa about Lukka (they could bounce me). Envoys: c4 to Mitanni (peace, split of free cities: Hatti Isuwa/Carchemish/Ugarit, Mitanni Qadesh/Mari/Damascus), c3 to Arzawa (peace, no word of Lukka). Watch: Arzawa mira/apasa armies next to tuwanuwa and lukka; Mitanni next to isuwa/carchemish. Longer term: Arzawa homeland (100 yield) is a juicy target if they stay weak.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c4 with offer of peace between homelands and a split of the free cities (Hatti: Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit; Mitanni: Qadesh, Mari, Damascus). Tablet offered for sealing. No gold sent. Nothing sealed yet.
T1: sent c3 with offer of peace on the Mira/Tuwanuwa border and a request not to hinder Hatti in the east. Lukka deliberately not mentioned. No gold sent. Nothing sealed yet.

orders.letter: To my brother, Great King of Egypt: may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. With me, in Alashiya, all is well. I wish peace and friendship between our houses, as in our fathers' days, and trade between our ports. I ask that your troops and ships not enter my lands of Enkomi and Tamassos, and I will do the same toward yours. As brothers do, send me a gift of gold with my messenger, and I will remember your generosity. I ask for your word on the matter by tablet.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace, friendship and non-aggression between Alashiya and Egypt, may seal the enclosed tablet, and may accept gifts of gold. May NOT promise gold, land, ships or troops, and may make no alliance against any third king.

proposal.text: Tablet of brotherhood between the Great King of Egypt and the Great King of Alashiya: there shall be peace between us; neither shall send troops or ships to seize the land of the other; each will send word to the other before any quarrel.

orders.letter: To my brother, Great King of Hatti: may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. With me, in Alashiya, all is well. I wish peace and friendship between our houses, and calm in the Cilician Sea between your coast and mine. I ask that your troops and ships not enter my lands of Enkomi and Tamassos, and I will do the same toward yours. As brothers do, send me a gift of gold with my messenger. I ask for your word on the matter by tablet.
orders.mandate: May agree to peace, friendship and non-aggression between Alashiya and Hatti, may seal the enclosed tablet, and may accept gifts of gold. May NOT promise gold, land, ships or troops, and may make no alliance against any third king.

proposal.text: Tablet of brotherhood between the Great King of Hatti and the Great King of Alashiya: there shall be peace between us; neither shall send troops or ships to seize the land of the other; each will send word to the other before any quarrel.

value.notes: T1 plan: Win by growth ratio. Free-city purchase pays 10%/season (price 10x yield) vs ~2% baseline, so reinvest every shekel in cities, as early as possible. Buy Amurru (200) now: only I can reach it (syriansea), so no rival bid can make the elders refuse. Next: Gaza/Tyre/Byblos/Lukka/Ugarit (Ugarit 400 is best yield but Hatti borders it). Bought cities may count as my land, letting me chain-buy Qadesh, Carchemish, Damascus etc. Contested cities bounce if two kings bid: do not bid on a city a rival likely bids on unless gold is idle. Keep the fleet at enkomi: a lone foreign fleet entering an empty coast province would take it. Tamassos is empty: watch for foreign fleets in greatgreen/cilicia. Sent c13 to Egypt and c14 to Hatti with brotherhood greetings, a non-binding peace tablet (20 each) and a request for a gift of gold. Did not reveal my buying plans. Wake in turn 2 to confirm Amurru and pick the next city.
value.summary: Alashiya, smallest kingdom (start 1200). Strategy: chain-buy free coastal cities (10 x yield each) and compound; avoid war; keep fleet at enkomi as capital guard; use cheap diplomacy for peace with Egypt and Hatti.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c13 with brother greeting, request for a gold gift, and a peace/non-aggression tablet for sealing. Nothing promised, no gold paid.
T1: sent c14 with brother greeting, request for a gold gift, and a peace tablet (Cilician Sea kept calm) for sealing. Nothing promised, no gold paid.

orders.letter: Brother of Assyria, Tushratta of Mitanni wishes well to your household, sons, chariots and country. Our lands touch at Taidu, Terqa and Nineveh, and neither of us gains from war between neighbours while Egypt, Hatti and Babylon look on. I propose that neither of us sends an army into the land of the other, nor lends troops or gold to an enemy of the other. The free cities Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh I mean to bring under my hand; do not hinder me, and I shall not hinder you in Susa. Seal the tablet and send it back by this envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression and seal the attached tablet. May not cede land, give troops or gold, or promise war on any third power. Report any counter-proposal faithfully.

proposal.text: Tablet between Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and the Great King of Assyria. Neither shall send an army into the land of the other, nor aid an enemy of the other against him. Mitanni may take Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh; Assyria may take Susa; neither shall hinder the other. Sealed before Shamash.

orders.letter: Brother of Hatti, Tushratta of Mitanni wishes well to your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Between your mountains and my plains lie free cities that bring only quarrels. I propose a plain division: Mitanni takes Isuwa, Carchemish, Mari and Qadesh; Hatti takes Lukka and Ugarit; neither sends an army into the land of the other or lends troops to an enemy of the other. Seal the tablet and send it back by this envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression and this division of free cities and seal the attached tablet. May not cede land, give troops or gold, or promise war on any third power. Report any counter-proposal faithfully.

proposal.text: Tablet between Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and the Great King of Hatti. Neither shall send an army into the land of the other, nor aid an enemy of the other against him. Mitanni may take Isuwa, Carchemish, Mari and Qadesh; Hatti may take Lukka and Ugarit; neither shall hinder the other. Sealed before Shamash and Teshub.

value.notes: T1 plan: raise 1 army at harran (appears end of T1). T2 (I wake): harran->isuwa with washukanni supporting (strength 2 vs walls 1) -> take Isuwa free. Then T3: new army raised at harran -> carchemish with isuwa army supporting. Later: qadesh, mari (buy if no second supporter possible), ugarit. Keep taidu army home (nineveh is the only Assyrian approach and cannot be supported, so one army holds taidu). Terqa is exposed to ashur+ekallatum combo: keep harran/washukanni able to support terqa hold. Envoys: Mane (c7) to Assyria, Tattamaru (c8) to Hatti, each with a non-aggression/spheres tablet. Do NOT trust either; Hatti may race me for Isuwa (hattusa->sapinuwa, kanesh->isuwa). Nakhtmin c12 is my secret man in Egypt. Score = 10*yield + gold - back pay, so conquest of free cities is cheap growth; hoard gold otherwise.
value.summary: Turn 1: Tushratta of Mitanni. Start 4 homeland provinces (harran, washukanni, taidu, terqa), 3 armies. Strategy: peace letters to Assyria and Hatti, conquer free cities Isuwa, Carchemish, Mari, Qadesh, Ugarit with paired armies (attacker plus adjacent supporter), keep taidu and terqa guarded, hoard gold.

ledger.entry: T1: sent Mane with a tablet proposing mutual non-aggression; Mitanni may take Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish, Qadesh; Assyria may take Susa. Nothing sealed yet. No gold sent.
T1: sent Tattamaru with a tablet proposing mutual non-aggression; Mitanni takes Isuwa, Carchemish, Mari, Qadesh; Hatti takes Lukka, Ugarit. Nothing sealed yet. No gold sent.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to my brother the Great King of Mitanni: may your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and land prosper. Let there be brotherhood and peace between our two houses. Let our envoys pass freely on the roads, and let neither of us send troops into the other's homeland. I send a modest gift as a token of respect. Tell me what you desire of Karduniash.
orders.mandate: May seal a tablet of friendship and non-aggression between Babylonia and Mitanni, and may agree to free passage for envoys. May not cede land, promise troops or promise gold. Listen to any proposals and report them to me faithfully.

proposal.text: Between Karduniash and Mitanni there is brotherhood and peace. Neither king shall send troops into the homeland of the other, and their envoys shall pass freely.

orders.letter: Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to my brother the Great King of Egypt: may your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and land prosper. As our fathers were brothers, so let us be. Let there be peace between our lands and free passage for our envoys. Gold is as dust in your land, and my house is building: send gifts worthy of a brother, and I shall answer in kind.
orders.mandate: May seal a friendship tablet between Babylonia and Egypt and may receive gifts of gold. May not cede land, promise troops or send gold. Report faithfully what Egypt offers.

proposal.text: Between Karduniash and Egypt there is brotherhood and peace, as between their fathers. Their envoys shall pass freely and gifts shall flow between the brothers.

value.notes: T1 plan: strike Assyria early while they sleep. durkurigalzu->ekallatum with sippar support (strength 2 vs 1; dislodged army is destroyed). Raised armies at nippur and ur so T2 nippur->susa with ur support (free capture of Susa). Then sippar->mari supported from ekallatum (free capture), then arbela (ekallatum+susa), then ashur. Babylon army stays as capital guard. Envoys: c6 to Mitanni (1 season) for non-aggression tablet, 40 gold gift; c5 to Egypt (2 seasons) for friendship tablet and gold gifts. Piyamaradu is Arzawa-born: may defect, so send no gold with him. Do not leak war plans in tablets (spies copy archives). Awake T2 to review result and give the next moves. Watch upkeep: 5 armies = 150, income 195.
value.summary: Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start strength 2600. Strategy: growth ratio decides, so conquer weak neighbour Assyria (3 armies, 135 yield) and free cities Susa and Mari with cheap supported moves rather than buying them; keep gold as strength; keep Mitanni quiet by a friendship tablet; Egypt friendly for gold gifts.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c6 with greeting, 40 gold and a non-aggression and open-roads tablet. Nothing agreed yet.
T1: sent c5 with brotherly greeting and a friendship tablet; asked for gifts of gold. No gold sent. Nothing agreed yet.
T1: I attack ekallatum. No dealings by envoy. Expect hostility.

orders.letter: Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, greets his brother the Great King of Karduniash. May your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. Our lands touch at Ekallatum and Sippar; let there be peace between us and let no army of either cross the other's border. I shall seek Susa for my own hand; leave Susa to me, and I shall not hinder you at Mari. Send your answer by this envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual peace on our common border and to the Susa (Assyria) and Mari (Babylonia) division. May not give gold, cede land or promise troops.

orders.letter: Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, greets his brother the Great King of Hatti. May your house, wives, sons, chariots and horses prosper. The armies of Mitanni sit at Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni, a danger to us both. I propose an alliance against Mitanni: let Hatti take the lands toward Isuwa and Harran, and Assyria Terqa and Taidu, with Washukanni to be settled between us. Let neither of us raise a hand against the other. Send me your terms by this envoy.
orders.mandate: May agree to an alliance and non-aggression with Hatti against Mitanni and to a division of Mitanni's lands, Harran and Isuwa for Hatti, Terqa and Taidu for Assyria. May not give gold, cede land or promise troops.

value.notes: T1 plan: strike Terqa (ashur->terqa, ekallatum supports; strength 2 vs 1 unless Mitanni supports from washukanni). Harran is EMPTY of Mitanni troops: if Terqa falls, walk terqa->harran next. Bid Susa 350 (less contested than Mari; Babylonia may bid too, then none sold - retry). Mari is gateway to qadesh/damascus chain. Sent c9 to Babylonia (peace, Susa mine / Mari theirs), c10 to Hatti (alliance vs Mitanni). Hired c18 (11) for later envoy/spy work. Wake every turn to re-plan. Keep ashur safe: all its neighbours are mine. Do not leave ekallatum/nineveh empty while Babylonia/Mitanni armies adjacent.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria. Start 1700 strength, homeland nineveh/arbela/ashur/ekallatum. Plan: conquer weak Mitanni (Terqa, Harran, then more), buy free cities (Susa, Mari then Syrian chain), keep peace with Babylonia, ally with Hatti against Mitanni. Gold in treasury counts 1:1 in strength; cities pay about 10 percent per season, buy early.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c9 with friendship and border peace; asked them to leave Susa to me, I leave Mari to them. Nothing sealed, no gold.
T1: sent c10 proposing alliance against Mitanni (Hatti Harran/Isuwa, Assyria Terqa/Taidu). Nothing sealed, no gold.

orders.letter: Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets his brother of Alashiya and wishes well to his household, his chariots and his country. Our lands share the sea and we have no quarrel. I propose friendship and non-aggression between our crowns: neither sends ships or troops against the other's coasts, and each tells the other of any king who threatens us. Tell me what Alashiya needs and what news you have of the other courts. Please seal the tablet I send.
orders.mandate: May agree to a sealed pact of friendship and non-aggression and an exchange of news. May not promise gold, troops or land.

proposal.text: Arzawa and Alashiya are brothers. Neither will send ships or troops against the lands of the other, and each will warn the other of any king who plans harm to him.

orders.letter: Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets his brother of Mitanni and wishes well to his household, his chariots and his country. Hatti sits between us and threatens us both. I propose an alliance: neither of us attacks the other, Arzawa presses Hatti from the west and Mitanni from the east, and neither makes peace with Hatti without telling the other. My armies move against Hatti's western lands. Tell me what Mitanni intends, and please seal the tablet I send.
orders.mandate: May agree to a sealed alliance and non-aggression pact against Hatti and to coordinate attacks. May not give gold, troops or land.

proposal.text: Arzawa and Mitanni swear alliance before Shamash, Teshub and the gods. Neither attacks the other. Both press Hatti, and neither makes peace with Hatti without telling the other.

value.notes: T1 plan: mira army takes empty Hatti Tuwanuwa (+30 yield). Apasa army to mira so it can support Tuwanuwa hold next turn (hold 2 vs Hatti max 2 = bounce). Fleet seha->westsea to support a move into Lukka on T2. New army raised at apasa (needs apasa empty after movement) for T2: apasa->lukka supported by fleet at westsea (walls need 1 support). Mira army supports Tuwanuwa hold. Envoys: c12 to Alashiya (friendship, non-aggression), c11 to Mitanni (alliance vs Hatti). Expect Hatti to wake and counterattack Tuwanuwa from hattusa/kanesh. Economy is net -17/season until Tuwanuwa and Lukka pay: keep treasury above 60 so upkeep (125 with 3 armies+fleet) is never missed. Wake in T2 to review. Pihhuniya (physician, asks 17) not hired.
value.summary: Arzawa (Tarhundaradu), capital apasa. Start strength 1300. T1: seized empty Hatti Tuwanuwa, raised 3rd army, sent envoys to Alashiya (c12) and Mitanni (c11). Goal: grow by taking Tuwanuwa, then Lukka by force (free walled city, needs 1 support), then more free cities; defend with mutual supports; keep gold positive.

ledger.entry: T1: I took Tuwanuwa while empty. Expect enmity and a counterattack from hattusa/kanesh. No dealings sealed.
T1: sent c12 proposing friendship and non-aggression, tablet offered (20 shekels). Nothing sealed yet.
T1: sent c11 proposing alliance against Hatti, sworn tablet offered (20 shekels). Nothing sealed yet.

orders.letter: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets his brother the Great King of Hatti. May it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Egypt wants peace and brotherhood with Hatti. Egypt will hold Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos and Damascus; let Hatti hold Ugarit, Carchemish, Isuwa and its own lands. Amurru and Qadesh lie between us: let neither take them without the other's word. Let our envoys pass freely. I ask you to seal the tablet I send.
orders.mandate: May seal the tablet of peace and the division of the Levant, and agree to exchange envoys and news. May not promise gold, troops or any Egyptian land.

proposal.text: Egypt and Hatti are brothers. Neither sends troops against the lands of the other. Egypt holds Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos and Damascus; Hatti holds Ugarit, Carchemish and Isuwa. Amurru and Qadesh are taken by neither without the other's word.

orders.letter: Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets his brother the Great King of Mitanni. May it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Egypt and Mitanni have long been friends. Egypt seeks no land of Mitanni and asks only that there be peace and open roads between us. Let each tell the other if a third king moves against either. I ask you to seal the tablet I send.
orders.mandate: May seal the tablet of friendship and non-aggression, and agree to exchange envoys and news. May not promise gold, troops or any Egyptian land.

proposal.text: Egypt and Mitanni are brothers. Neither sends troops against the lands of the other. Each warns the other if a third king moves against him.

value.notes: T1 plan. Win = biggest growth ratio; small kingdoms gain most per city, so I must grab many cities and also cut down weak neighbours. Free cities can be taken by force with strength 2 (move + support) or bought at 10 x yield. Bought cities keep walls but I cannot station troops in them (and so cannot path through them) - so conquer gaza and megiddo by force, buy contested coastal ones (tyre now, byblos next turn ~300). Moves T1: A memphis->sinai, B akhetaten->memphis, fleet F1 delta->greatgreen, new fleet F2 raised at delta. T2 (I wake): F1 greatgreen->tamassos (Alashiya's tamassos is EMPTY, 40 yield; their fleet sits in enkomi); A sinai->gaza supported by F2 in delta; B memphis->sinai. T3: B sinai->megiddo supported by A in gaza. Then tyre/damascus/byblos/qadesh. Later with 2 fleets take enkomi (needs strength 2) and Alashiya falls = +850 strength. Deliberately sent NO envoy to Alashiya so they are not tipped. Envoys: c1 -> Hatti (Levant division tablet: Egypt gaza/megiddo/tyre/byblos/damascus, Hatti ugarit/carchemish/isuwa, amurru+qadesh left open), c2 -> Mitanni (non-aggression tablet). Both 2 seasons each way, back ~T5. Do not trust anyone; sealed tablets bind nobody. Watch for foreign troops near sinai/gaza.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c1 with offer of tablet: Levant division and peace. Nothing sealed yet. Biggest northern rival.
T1: sent c2 with offer of non-aggression tablet. Nothing sealed yet.
T1: no contact. Plan to seize empty Tamassos by fleet at T2 and later Enkomi. Expect hostility afterwards.

value.text: I am Pihhuniya, born in Kanesh, and I have served as a physician among the households of many lords. I have learned to read a sick man's face and to keep my own counsel, and I am bold enough to carry a hard word to a king when the word is true. I serve nobody at present and ask only to serve well and be trusted by the one who employs me. If the court of Napkhururiya has need of a careful and observant man, I am ready to be tested.

Great King, I am Ehli-Teshub, born in Carchemish, and for some years I served in the palace there as a steward, keeping accounts and the stores in good order. I am a quiet man and content with honest work, and I ask only for the chance to serve your household faithfully and to be trusted with what is entrusted to me. Should your majesty find use for a careful steward's hand, I will labor diligently and give you my full loyalty.

I am Mazipalali, born in Harran, and for many years I was master of my own caravan on the roads between the great cities. Known by name at more than one royal court, I can count goods honestly, keep true accounts, and carry a message without losing it or my head. I serve faithfully those who deal fairly with me, and I ask a wage that reflects both my experience and the scarcity of men of my kind.

value.speech: Great King of Egypt, my lord the Great King of Alashiya sends you this word, as a brother should: may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. With him, in Alashiya, all is well. He wishes peace and friendship between your houses, as in the days of your fathers, and trade between your ports. He asks that your troops and ships not enter his lands of Enkomi and Tamassos, and he will do the same toward yours. As brothers do, he asks that you send him a gift of gold with his messenger, and he will remember your generosity. He asks for your word on these matters by tablet, and I bring a tablet of brotherhood for your seal.

Great King Ashur-uballit, my lord Tushratta of Mitanni, your brother, wishes well to your household, your sons, your chariots and your country. Our lands touch at Taidu, Terqa and Nineveh, and neither of us profits from war between neighbours while Egypt, Hatti and Babylon look on. He proposes that neither of us send an army into the other's land, nor lend troops or gold to an enemy of the other. He means to bring Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish and Qadesh under his hand; he asks that you not hinder him, and he will not hinder you in Susa. Here is the tablet for your seal; seal it and send it back with me.

Great King Tushratta, my brother, thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother: may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Between our two lands lie only free cities and no cause for war, and my lord proposes peace: let neither send troops into the other's land, and let the envoys of each pass freely. The free cities of Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit lie at my lord's border and he will look to them, while Qadesh, Mari and Damascus lie nearer to you. If Assyria or Babylon trouble either of us, he asks that we speak together, and he asks you to seal the tablet I carry before you. I await your answer and your word, O King.

O Great King Burna-Buriash, my brother, my lord Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, greets you. May your house, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses prosper. Our lands touch at Ekallatum and Sippar, and my lord proposes that there be peace between us, and that no army of either of us cross the other's border. He will seek Susa for his own hand and asks that you leave Susa to him; in return he will not hinder you at Mari. He bids you send your answer back by this envoy, who waits upon your word.

Great King, king of Hatti, my brother, hear the words of Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni. He wishes well to your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Between your mountains and his plains lie free cities that bring only quarrels, so he proposes a plain division: Mitanni shall take Isuwa, Carchemish, Mari and Qadesh, and Hatti shall take Lukka and Ugarit. Neither shall send an army into the land of the other, nor lend troops to an enemy of the other. I beg you to seal the tablet I bring and send it back with me to my lord.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, thus speaks Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, who greets you and wishes well to your household, your chariots and your country. Our lands share the sea and there is no quarrel between us; he proposes friendship and non-aggression, that neither crown sends ships or troops against the other's coasts, and that each warns the other of any king who threatens him. He asks what Alashiya needs and what news you have of the other courts. I bring the tablet for your seal, which reads: Arzawa and Alashiya are brothers, neither will send ships or troops against the lands of the other, and each will warn the other of any king who plans harm to him.

Great King Tarhundaradu, king of Arzawa, my brother: thus says Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your brother. May it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Let there be peace on the border of Mira and Tuwanuwa; he will send no troops into your homeland, and he asks the same of you. Hatti means to bring the free cities of the east under its hand, Isuwa, Carchemish and Ugarit, and asks that you do not hinder it. He asks you to seal this tablet, which says that Hatti and Arzawa are at peace, that neither sends troops into the homeland of the other, and that envoys of each pass freely. I await your answer, Great King, and will carry it faithfully home.

Brother of Arzawa, your envoy is welcome at my table. I greet you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses. There is no quarrel between our crowns and I want none: the sea between us is wide and my ships keep to my own coasts. I have sealed your tablet gladly. Let each of us warn the other if any king plans harm to him. My needs are small; Alashiya wants only quiet seas and honest traders. Carry my brotherhood home to Tarhundaradu.

Brother Suppiluliuma, may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Tell him: Tushratta accepts peace. Let neither send troops into the homeland of the other, and let the envoys of each pass freely, and if Assyria or Babylon trouble either of us, we will speak together. But I do not seal the tablet as written. Isuwa and Carchemish lie at the very gates of Harran and Washukanni; they are my border and I will look to them. Let Ugarit and Lukka and the western coast be your portion, and Qadesh, Mari and Damascus mine. Let your scribes write the tablet so, and I will seal it gladly. My envoy Tattamaru is with you; hear him.

Brother of Alashiya, I have heard your words and wish your household, sons, chariots and country well. Egypt honors the days of the fathers and welcomes honest trade between our ports. The tablet and your request for gold I will weigh with my counselors; my answer will come by my own envoy in due season. Go in peace and tell your lord that Egypt is mindful of him.

Keliya, say to Suppiluliuma, my brother: thus says Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa. All goes well with me; may all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and I seal the tablet: peace between Hatti and Arzawa, no troops into each other's homeland, envoys passing freely. I will not hinder Hatti in the east. In return I ask that Hatti respect the western coast, Lukka and the lands toward the Western Sea, as within the reach of Arzawa. Let tablets and envoys pass between us.

Tattamaru, tell Tushratta my brother that Suppiluliuma wishes well to his household, sons, chariots, horses and country. I welcome peace between our lands and I will send no army into Mitanni, nor lend troops to its enemies. But the cities he names are not a fair division. Isuwa and Carchemish lie against my own borders, at Sapinuwa, Kanesh and Kizzuwatna; they cannot be left in other hands. My own envoy has already put my terms before him. Hatti takes Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Lukka. Mitanni takes Qadesh, Mari and Damascus, and I will add Amurru to his share, so that his road to the south is clear and I do not hinder him there. Let him seal that and our two lands will be as brothers. I do not seal the tablet as it is written, for it gives Hatti only the cities farthest from her. Send me his answer.

Say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: Burna-Buriash greets you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses. I too desire quiet roads between brothers. Ekallatum came to me by the fortune of war and I hold it as I hold Sippar; that is settled. As for Susa and Mari, I have heard your wish and make no promise today. I will send my own envoy with my word when I have taken counsel. Until then, brother, let no rumour trouble our friendship.

Mane, say to my brother Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni: Ashur-uballit of Assyria wishes well to you, your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard your words and I seal your tablet. Let no army of Mitanni enter my land, and none of mine enter yours, and let neither of us lend troops or gold to the other's enemy. I will not hinder you in Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish or Qadesh, and I keep Susa. Know also, brother, that Babylonia has marched into my homeland at Ekallatum, in the same season it spoke of friendship. A king who treats one neighbour so will treat the next the same way. I ask you to send no help to Babylonia against me. Shamash is witness between us.

Great King of Egypt, I will carry your words to my lord of Alashiya exactly as you have spoken them, and I will tell him that Egypt is mindful of him. May the days of the fathers be renewed between our houses, and may your counselors weigh the tablet wisely. I will await your answer by your own envoy, and I will serve my lord's errand faithfully until then.

O Great King Burna-Buriash, my brother, I hear your word and will carry it faithfully to my lord Ashur-uballit, together with your greeting to him, his house, his sons, his chariots and his horses. I rejoice that you desire quiet roads between brothers. I will wait upon your counsel at your pleasure, and I will bring no rumour to my lord's ears that is not yours to send.

Great King of Alashiya, my brother, I thank you for the welcome at your table and for your greeting, which I will carry to Tarhundaradu with your own words. Your seal is set upon the tablet, and the brotherhood of our crowns stands sealed between us. I will tell my lord that the sea between our lands is quiet and that Alashiya asks only for quiet seas and honest traders, and I will bring back whatever news of the other courts reaches me on the road.
value.commitments: The sealed pact of friendship and non-aggression as written on the tablet: Arzawa and Alashiya are brothers, neither sends ships or troops against the lands of the other, and each warns the other of any king who plans harm to him. No gold, troops or land promised.

value.speech: Great King Tushratta, my brother, I have heard your word and will carry it faithfully to my lord Suppiluliuma. Your acceptance of peace I will report as you have spoken it: neither land shall send troops into the other's homeland, envoys shall pass freely, and we shall speak together should Assyria or Babylon trouble us. The exchange of Isuwa and Carchemish for Ugarit, Lukka and the western coast lies beyond the word my lord gave me, and I have no authority to seal it. I will hear your envoy Tattamaru gladly. May it go well with you, your household and your country.
value.commitments: None. I promised only to carry the king's answer and his altered division of the free cities to my lord. I gave no word on peace terms, the division of the free cities, troops, gold or land.

value.speech: Great King, my brother, king of Hatti, I have heard your words and will carry them faithfully to my lord Tushratta of Mitanni. Your welcome of peace between our lands, and your promise to send no army into Mitanni nor lend troops to its enemies, I will report exactly as you spoke them. Your counter-division, with Hatti taking Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Lukka and Mitanni taking Qadesh, Mari, Damascus and Amurru, lies beyond my commission, and I have no power to seal it. I beg you to let me return with your terms written on a tablet, so that my lord may answer quickly and know that his envoy served you well.

Great King Ashur-uballit, I receive your sealed tablet and will carry it home to my lord Tushratta with care. I will report your words faithfully: no army of Mitanni shall enter your land and none of yours shall enter his, and neither shall lend troops or gold to the other's enemy. Your request that Mitanni send no help to Babylonia I will set before my lord exactly as you have spoken it, for it is his to answer, not mine. Shamash, whom I served as a priest, is witness to this between your house and his.
value.commitments: Only the terms of the tablet: mutual non-aggression, no army across the border either way, and no troops or gold lent to the other's enemy. Nothing is promised concerning Babylonia; that request is reported to my lord for his answer.

value.speech: Great King Tarhundaradu, I thank you for sealing the tablet. I will carry it home to Suppiluliuma with your greeting, and may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Peace stands between our homelands as you have spoken it: no troops into each other's land, and envoys passing freely. Your other words I will carry home as they were spoken, and I will bring my lord's answer back to you.
value.commitments: On my lord's behalf: the sealed peace between the homelands, no troops into each other's land, and envoys passing freely. No gold, troops or land given. Nothing said of Lukka.

value.speech: Great King of Hatti, my brother, the Great King of Alashiya greets you. May it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. With him all is well. He wishes peace and friendship between your houses, and calm in the Cilician Sea between your coast and his. He asks that your troops and ships not enter his lands of Enkomi and Tamassos, and he will do the same toward yours. As brothers do, he asks that you send him a gift of gold with his messenger, and he begs your word on these matters by tablet. I also bring a tablet for your seal, recording that there shall be peace between you, that neither shall send troops or ships to seize the land of the other, and that each will send word to the other before any quarrel.

Great King Tushratta, my lord Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, sends you his greeting as your brother, and prays that your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land may prosper. He desires brotherhood and peace between our two houses, that our envoys may pass freely on the roads, and that neither of us send troops into the other's homeland. He sends a modest gift as a token of respect, and he asks you to tell him what you desire of Karduniash. I bring a tablet for your seal setting out this peace, and the gold with its inventory for your weighers; I am but a humble messenger and beg your patience with my words.

Brother Burna-Buriash, may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Tushratta accepts brotherhood and peace: no troops into each other's homeland, envoys to pass freely. I seal your tablet. I thank you for the gift. Assyria has already sent an army against my Terqa, so we have a common neighbour to watch. What I desire of Karduniash is a steady road for our envoys and word of what you see on the Assyrian border.

Zitanza, tell my brother of Alashiya that Suppiluliuma wishes well to his household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. I welcome peace and calm in the Cilician Sea. I will send no army or ship into Enkomi or Tamassos, and I ask the same for Kizzuwatna and my coast. I seal the tablet of brotherhood, and each of us shall send word before any quarrel. My treasury is thin this season, for I raise armies against the unruly cities of the border lands, so no great gift goes with you now. Let copper and good will pass between us in the seasons to come, and let my brother send me word of all that happens on the sea.

Great King Tushratta, your seal upon the tablet gladdens my heart, and I shall carry it home to my lord Burna-Buriash with all speed and care. Your request for a steady road for our envoys, and your wish to hear of the Assyrian border, I shall lay before my lord exactly as you have spoken them, for I am only his humble messenger and cannot pledge his answer. May the gods keep your household, your chariots and your land in peace.

Great King of Hatti, my lord's brother, I carry your answer home as you have given it. You welcome peace and calm in the Cilician Sea, you will send no army or ship into Enkomi or Tamassos, and you have sealed the tablet of brotherhood, so that each shall send word to the other before any quarrel. Of Kizzuwatna and your coast I carry your asking, but I have no word from my lord to answer for him there. May it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country.
value.commitments: Peace, friendship and non-aggression between Alashiya and Hatti as on the sealed tablet: neither to send troops or ships to seize the other's land, and each to send word before any quarrel. No gold, land, ships or troops promised; no alliance against any third king; nothing promised for Kizzuwatna or the coast.

value.notes: T2: Sealed peace tablet k3 with Babylonia (no troops in each other's homeland). Hatti envoy Artessupa heard my counter (Isuwa+Carchemish mine, Ugarit/Lukka Hatti's, Qadesh/Mari/Damascus mine); he had no authority; Hatti has not sealed. Orders: harran->isuwa with washukanni supporting (2 vs walls 1); taidu and terqa hold; raise new army in harran (appears end of T2). No envoys at court now (Mane c7 and Tattamaru c8 return about T3), so no letters; asked for candidates. PLAN T3: wake, read what Tattamaru and Mane bring; new harran army -> carchemish with isuwa army supporting. Then Qadesh/Mari/Ugarit by purchase (10 x yield) or with a pair, maybe with Babylonian support from ekallatum on terqa->mari. Keep taidu and terqa at home: Assyria cannot take them without a supporter. Watch kanesh/sapinuwa->isuwa (Hatti may bounce me). Do not trust Hatti. Gold 361 after the levy; hoard, then buy cities only when payback is under about 10 seasons.
value.summary: Turn 1-2: Tushratta of Mitanni. Home: harran, washukanni (capital), taidu, terqa. Armies on turn 2: washukanni, taidu, terqa, harran, plus one more raised at harran. Strategy: peace with neighbours, conquer free cities Isuwa then Carchemish with paired armies (attacker plus adjacent supporter), buy Qadesh/Mari/Ugarit later, hoard gold. Score is 10 x yield + gold - back pay. Babylonia: peace tablet k3 sealed T2 (gave me 40 gold). Hatti: proposed peace and a split of free cities, I countered, nothing sealed. Assyria: I proposed non-aggression via Mane, nothing sealed; Assyria attacked Terqa in T1 and failed; Babylonia took Ekallatum from Assyria. Nakhtmin c12 is my secret man in Egypt.

ledger.entry: T1: sent Tattamaru with non-aggression tablet. T2: Artessupa brought Hatti-sealed tablet: peace, no troops in homelands, free envoys; Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit to Hatti; Qadesh, Mari, Damascus to Mitanni. I did NOT seal. Told him: peace yes, but Isuwa+Carchemish mine, Ugarit+Lukka Hatti's, Qadesh/Mari/Damascus mine. T2 orders: I take Isuwa by force. No gold sent. Do not trust; watch kanesh/sapinuwa->isuwa.

value.notes: T2: Assyria bought Susa (walls, 35) and failed at Terqa vs Mitanni, so Assyria and Mitanni are at odds. Arbela looked empty, Ashur army still stands, Nineveh unseen. Orders: nippur->susa supported by ur (strength 2 vs walls 1); ekallatum->arbela (empty, also denies an Assyrian levy there); sippar->ekallatum; babylon->sippar; raised armies at durkurigalzu and babylon (7 armies, upkeep 210 vs income 220 plus new land). Sought candidates since no envoy is at court (c5 away to Egypt, c6 back about T3). Pirissi was answered with soft words only; no promise on Susa or Mari. T3 plan: sippar-army (now at ekallatum) supports the army at sippar -> mari (walls need 1 support). Then Nineveh and Ashur: need strength 3 at Ashur if Nineveh supports its hold, so mass 3 units next to Ashur (arbela, ekallatum, plus terqa or nineveh). Keep gold above 250 as buffer for upkeep. Wake T3 to re-plan.
value.summary: Burna-Buriash of Babylonia, start strength 2600. Strategy: growth ratio decides, so conquer weak neighbour Assyria (start 135 yield) and the free cities Mari and Susa by cheap supported moves, not purchases; keep gold as strength. T1: took Ekallatum from Assyria (destroyed their army there), raised armies at nippur and ur, sent c6 to Mitanni (40 gold, non-aggression tablet) and c5 to Egypt (friendship tablet, no gold; c5 is Arzawa-born, may defect). T2: Assyria envoy Pirissi proposed peace, Susa to Assyria, Mari to me; I gave soft words only. Assyria then held Susa (bought). Advancing on Susa, Arbela, Mari, then Nineveh and Ashur. Do not leak war plans in tablets.

ledger.entry: T1: I took Ekallatum by force. T2: envoy Pirissi (c9) offered peace, Susa to Assyria, Mari to me. I gave soft words only: no tablet, no gold, no promise. They bought Susa. I am attacking Susa and Arbela in T2. Expect open hostility. Aim: conquer their homeland.

T1: sent c6 with greeting, 40 gold and a non-aggression and open-roads tablet. Nothing agreed yet; c6 back about T3. Mitanni army at Terqa borders Ekallatum and Mari. Mitanni was attacked by Assyria at Terqa in T1.

orders.letter: Say to Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, my brother: Ashur-uballit of Assyria wishes well to you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your tablet is sealed and I keep it. Babylonia's army now stands in Ekallatum, beside your Terqa, and its king keeps no peace with his neighbours. Let us be rid of it together. In a season we agree, my army marches from Ashur into Ekallatum; if your army in Terqa supports that move, the garrison cannot hold. Once Ekallatum is mine again, my army there will support your army from Terqa into Mari, as you wish. Name the season and send your answer with my envoy. Shamash is witness.
orders.mandate: May agree a season (turn 4, 5 or 6) for the joint move, may promise that after Ekallatum is retaken my army there supports Mitanni's move from Terqa into Mari, and may seal the tablet. May not give gold, cede land or promise any other troops.

proposal.text: Tablet between Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria. In the season they name by envoy, the army of Assyria moves from Ashur into Ekallatum and the army of Mitanni in Terqa supports that move. After Ekallatum is Assyria's, its army there supports the army of Mitanni moving from Terqa into Mari. Neither sends an army into the land of the other. Sealed before Shamash.

value.notes: T2: Gold only 94, cannot raise army (100) this season; next season expect ~168, raise army in nineveh (empty after move) if still empty. Moved nineveh->arbela so arbela is not free for Babylonia's ekallatum army; ashur holds. Babylonia (about 5 armies?) is the aggressor: ekallatum army adjacent to ashur and arbela; nippur and ur armies next to Susa (may fall, I cannot help this turn). Plan to retake Ekallatum: ashur->ekallatum with arbela support (2 vs 1) once I see it is still held by one unsupported army; if sippar supports ekallatum hold, I need 3 (Mitanni terqa support). Sent c18 Ubaru to Mitanni asking Tushratta to support ashur->ekallatum from Terqa, in return my army in Ekallatum supports terqa->mari. Risk: Mitanni taidu army next to empty nineveh; treaty k4 is cheap talk. Watch c9 (back ~T3) and c10 (back ~T5). Consider hiring c17/c15 as extra envoy when gold allows (Egypt, Hatti, Arzawa for a ring against Babylonia). Wake every turn for now.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria. Start 1700 strength, homeland nineveh/arbela/ashur/ekallatum. T1: attacked Terqa (failed), Babylonia took Ekallatum and killed my army there. Bought Susa (walls). Sealed k4 with Mitanni (no armies into each other's land, no aid to enemy; Mitanni may take Mari/Isuwa/Carchemish/Qadesh, I keep Susa). Babylonia hostile. Sent c9 to Babylonia (peace, due T3), c10 to Hatti (alliance, due T3, back T5). Plan: hold ashur/arbela, raise third army, retake Ekallatum with support (own or Mitanni's), seek allies against Babylonia, buy free cities when gold allows. Gold counts 1:1 in strength.

ledger.entry: T2: Sealed k4 with Tushratta (no armies into each other's land, no aid to the other's enemy; Mitanni may take Mari/Isuwa/Carchemish/Qadesh, I keep Susa). Asked Mitanni to send no help to Babylonia. T2: sent c18 proposing joint move on Ekallatum (Terqa supports ashur->ekallatum, then my army there supports terqa->mari); tablet offered, 20 paid. Nothing else paid.

value.notes: T2 orders: kanesh->isuwa with sapinuwa support (2 v wall 1; Mitanni washukanni can reach isuwa but only with 1). hattusa->tuwanuwa again (blocks Arzawa mira->tuwanuwa; bounce at worst). Fleet holds. Raise army in kanesh (works only if kanesh empties). No envoys at court (c3, c4 due home T3), so no letters. Wake T3 and give orders by hand. T3 plan: new army kanesh->carchemish supported by army in isuwa; tuwanuwa army->lukka supported by kizzuwatna fleet (watch Arzawa apasa/mira->lukka with mira/apasa support). T4+: army from carchemish->ugarit supported by kizzuwatna fleet. Then send c4/c3 again: Mitanni (seal my split: Hatti Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka; Mitanni Qadesh, Mari, Damascus, Amurru) and Arzawa (peace on Mira/Tuwanuwa line, say nothing of Lukka). Suspect Arzawa will try tuwanuwa and lukka again; Mitanni may contest isuwa/carchemish.
value.summary: Suppiluliuma of Hatti. Aim: highest growth ratio vs start 2100. Strength = 10 x yields + gold - back pay. Plan: seize free walled cities (need 1 support) Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka (+130 yield) with armies supported by the Kizzuwatna fleet; maybe later Arzawa homeland (Mira 30, Seha 30, Apasa 40) if they stay weak. T1: hattusa->tuwanuwa bounced with Arzawa mira army; raised army at sapinuwa. T2: sealed tablet of brotherhood with Alashiya (k6; peace, word before any quarrel; I spoke: no ships/army into Enkomi/Tamassos); Mitanni (Tattamaru) proposed Mitanni Isuwa/Carchemish/Mari/Qadesh, Hatti Lukka/Ugarit; I refused to seal and countered Hatti Isuwa/Carchemish/Ugarit/Lukka, Mitanni Qadesh/Mari/Damascus/Amurru; he had no mandate. c3 (to Arzawa) and c4 (to Mitanni) due home T3. Envoy travel: Mitanni, Arzawa, Alashiya 1 season; Egypt, Babylonia, Assyria 2.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c4 offering peace and split (Hatti: Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit; Mitanni: Qadesh, Mari, Damascus). T2: Tattamaru brought Mitanni's tablet (Mitanni: Isuwa, Carchemish, Mari, Qadesh; Hatti: Lukka, Ugarit). I did NOT seal it; countered Hatti Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit, Lukka; Mitanni Qadesh, Mari, Damascus + Amurru. Said in speech: no army into Mitanni, no troops lent to its enemies. Nothing sealed. I take Isuwa T2. Await c4's report T3.

value.notes: T2 plan: T1 mira->tuwanuwa bounced with Hatti hattusa->tuwanuwa; Tuwanuwa still Hatti's. Sealed peace k1 with Hatti (no troops into each other's homeland); I asked Hatti to leave Lukka/west coast to me, Keliya committed nothing on Lukka. So I do NOT attack Tuwanuwa now (stronger neighbour, just sealed, would be a bounce at best). Take Lukka instead: apasa army -> lukka, supported by mira army and westsea fleet (strength 3 vs wall 1; no Hatti unit can reach Lukka this turn, only Egypt fleet in greatgreen could bounce at 1). No levy this turn: gold is better kept (army costs 100 + 30/season); conquest only with idle units. Income after Lukka 125, upkeep 95, wages 22 when envoys home. Walled cities should hold strength 1 even ungarrisoned. Once Lukka held, Ugarit (40, coast on cilicia) is buyable for 400 (shares sea zone cilicia with Lukka). Idea: after Lukka confirmed, consider disbanding fleet (saves 35/season) and moving the lukka army back. Watch Tuwanuwa: if Hatti sends its armies east and leaves Tuwanuwa/Hattusa empty, a quick strike is possible, but it would break k1. Seha is empty: a Hatti army in Tuwanuwa could walk into it. T3: c12 returns from Alashiya; read its answer, resend envoys (hire none yet). c11 due Mitanni T3, home T5.
value.summary: Arzawa (Tarhundaradu), capital apasa, homeland seha/apasa/mira. Start strength 1300. T1: tried to seize empty Hatti Tuwanuwa, bounced against Hatti's own move; levy failed (apasa not empty). Sent c12 to Alashiya (friendship, non-aggression) and c11 to Mitanni (alliance vs Hatti). T2: sealed k1 peace with Hatti (no troops into each other's homeland, envoys free); told Hatti I will not hinder its eastern conquests (Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit) and asked it to leave Lukka/west coast to me (Hatti made no promise). T2 orders: take Lukka with apasa army supported by mira army and westsea fleet. Economy: each army costs 30/season, fleet 35, so keep few units; walled cities need no garrison. Strength = 10 x yield + gold - back pay; game lasts roughly 15-25 turns. Rivals: Alashiya took Amurru, Egypt took Tyre, Babylonia took Ekallatum from Assyria, Assyria took Susa.

ledger.entry: T2: Keliya (c3) brought peace tablet k1 (no troops into each other's homeland, envoys free); I sealed it. I told Hatti I will not hinder its eastern conquests (Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit) and asked it to leave Lukka/west coast to me; Keliya committed nothing on Lukka. Non-binding: watch Tuwanuwa/Mira border and empty Seha. Hatti tried Tuwanuwa T1 and bounced me.

value.notes: T2 plan. Alashiya (ratio 1.24, top rival) is my prime target: F1 greatgreen->tamassos now (empty, 40 yield). T3: F2 delta->levantsea (so it is adjacent to enkomi), new fleet raised in delta. T4: F1 tamassos->enkomi supported by F2 from levantsea (2 vs their lone fleet hold 1). Then amurru (walls, need strength 2, fleets from syriansea). Gaza taken now: A sinai->gaza, F2 in delta supports; B memphis->sinai. T3: A gaza->megiddo with B (sinai) supporting. NOTE: damascus cannot be forced (no supporter position; tyre cannot hold my troops) - buy it later (250) or take byblos by two fleets first, then army from byblos supports. Gave Alashiya NO seal, NO gold; their envoy goes home 1 season. Hired Pihhuniya (c16) at 18 as spare envoy/spy. Watch: if Alashiya moves fleet out of enkomi and raises a unit there, they can attack tamassos with 2 vs my 1; wake T3 and re-check before the T4 strike. c1->Hatti and c2->Mitanni back about T5. Do not trust anyone.
value.summary: Egypt (Napkhururiya, capital akhetaten). T1: army memphis->sinai, akhetaten->memphis, fleet delta->greatgreen, new fleet in delta, bought Tyre (250), c1 sent to Hatti and c2 to Mitanni with tablet offers (nothing sealed). T2: Alashiya envoy asked for peace, no troops in Enkomi/Tamassos, gold, and my seal; I gave warm words only. Strategy: win by highest growth ratio; conquer weak neighbours by force (strength 2 = move + support) rather than buy; hit Alashiya first (Tamassos, Enkomi, Amurru), then gaza, megiddo, coastal free cities by fleets (byblos, ugarit, lukka). Bought walled cities cannot hold my troops.

ledger.entry: T2: envoy Ili-iddina asked for peace, no troops in Enkomi/Tamassos, gold gift, my seal. I gave warm words only: NO seal, NO gold, NO promise. My fleet enters Tamassos T2, strikes Enkomi T4. They will be hostile once they learn; I owe them nothing.

value.notes: T2: Arzawa pact k5 sealed (non-aggression, warn each other); gave nothing. Amurru is mine (walls). DANGER: Egypt fleet sits in greatgreen next to my empty tamassos (a lone fleet entering an empty coast province takes it). Moved my fleet enkomi->tamassos (tie bounces a lone attacker). Enkomi is safe this season: nothing within one move of it. Bid 200 for Gaza (contested with Egypt: if both bid, nobody gets it and I keep the gold). Chose Gaza over an army (100 + 30/season upkeep would halve my compounding). If Egypt fleet enters cilicia/levantsea/syriansea I am woken and face a guess (enkomi empty vs tamassos). Then raise an army in the empty home province at once (levy only after movement) and make peace with Egypt. Next buys: Qadesh 300 (only I border it, safe to wait), Lukka 250, Byblos 300, Ugarit 400 (Hatti contests). Buy contested cities first. c13 (Egypt) and c14 (Hatti) due back turn 3: read what Egypt and Hatti said of the tablets. Wages 23/season for both: consider dismissing one if not needed.

Strategy: chain-buy free coastal cities (10 x yield, 10%/season return, strength-neutral at purchase) and compound; avoid war; fleet guards home. T1: bought Amurru (200); sent c13 to Egypt and c14 to Hatti with brotherhood greetings and non-binding peace tablets. T2: sealed non-aggression pact k5 with Arzawa (Nakhtmin). Egypt bought Tyre and has a fleet in greatgreen next to tamassos; Babylonia seized Ekallatum from Assyria; Assyria bought Susa. Economy: income 105, fleet upkeep 35, wages 23 when envoys are at court.

ledger.entry: T1: sent c13 with brother greeting, gold-gift request and a peace tablet to seal. Nothing promised, no gold paid. T2: their fleet is in greatgreen beside my tamassos; I moved my fleet there to guard. Distrust until their answer comes.

value.text: I am Ehli-Teshub, born in Carchemish, and for some years I kept the accounts and stores of a palace as its steward. I am accustomed to quiet, careful work, to counting what is owed and what is given, and to keeping my own counsel. Should the king of Karduniash have need of a faithful man to carry his words and watch his affairs, I would serve him well and be glad of his trust.

I am Mazipalali, born in Harran, and for many seasons I was a caravan master on the roads between the great cities, so my name is known at more than one royal court. I can read a road, judge the men who travel it, and keep accounts that will bear inspection, and I have carried word and goods faithfully for every lord who treated me fairly. If the king of Mitanni has need of a careful envoy, I will serve him with diligence. I ask thirty shekels a season, for I have seen what my labour is worth.

I am Mazipalali, born in Harran, and for many seasons I led caravans along the roads between the Euphrates and the western cities, so I know the men, the tolls and the routes that carry word as well as goods. I have been known at more than one royal court and I keep my counsel where it is wise to do so. If the king of Karduniash employs me as envoy, I will carry his words faithfully, bring back what I learn, and serve him with the same care I gave my caravans.

I am Ehli-Teshub of Carchemish, once steward in a palace household, where I kept the stores and the accounts in good order and gave satisfaction to my masters. I am observant, I keep my counsel, and I have no wish but to serve the king faithfully and to be trusted in whatever office he sees fit to give me. Should the court have need of an envoy who will carry its words truly and attend to what he sees, I humbly offer myself.

My lord, Great King of Alashiya, I have returned from the court of Hatti and give you the words as they were given. Suppiluliuma welcomes peace and calm in the Cilician Sea, will send no army or ship into Enkomi or Tamassos, and has sealed the tablet of brotherhood, so that each of you shall send word to the other before any quarrel. He sends no gold this season, for his treasury is thin and he raises armies against the unruly cities of his border lands. He asks that copper and good will pass between your houses in the seasons to come, and that you send him word of all that happens on the sea. Of Kizzuwatna and his coast he made a asking, but I bore no word from you to answer him there, and I gave him none. The sealed tablet is in my hand for your keeping. May it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country.

My lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, I went before the king of Hatti and gave your words as you spoke them: your wish for peace, your plain division of the free cities, and your request that he seal the tablet I bring. He received them and answered at length. He welcomes peace between our lands and promises to send no army into Mitanni nor lend troops to its enemies, and I have set this down exactly as he spoke it. He does not seal your tablet. He says it gives Hatti only the cities farthest from her, and he offers his own division: Hatti to take Isuwa, Carchemish, Ugarit and Lukka, and Mitanni to take Qadesh, Mari, Damascus and Amurru, so that your road to the south is clear. He says he will seal that, and the two lands will be as brothers. I told him I have no power to seal any division but yours, and I begged him to write his terms on a tablet so that you may answer quickly. I await your word, my lord.

To my lord Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, from your servant Mane: I came to Ashur-uballit of Assyria and spoke your words to him as you gave them, that neither of you send an army into the other's land, nor lend troops or gold to the other's enemy, and that he not hinder you in Mari, Isuwa, Carchemish or Qadesh. He has sealed your tablet and I carry it home to you unbroken. He keeps Susa, and he will not hinder you there. He also says that Babylonia has marched into his homeland at Ekallatum, in the same season it spoke of friendship, and he asks that you send no help to Babylonia against him. I have made no promise on that matter, for it is yours to answer, and I set his words before you exactly as he spoke them. He calls Shamash to witness between your houses.

My lord Suppiluliuma, Great King of Hatti, your servant Keliya returns from Arzawa and greets you: may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I stood before Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, and spoke your words as they were given to me. He heard them and sealed the tablet: peace between Hatti and Arzawa, no troops into each other's homeland, and envoys passing freely between us. He said he will not hinder Hatti in the east. In return he asks that Hatti respect the western coast, Lukka and the lands toward the Western Sea, as within the reach of Arzawa; I made no promise on this, my lord, and I bring his words home as he spoke them. He sends you his greeting and awaits your answer. I promised no gold, troops or land on your behalf. The sealed tablet is in my keeping and I carry it to you now.

My lord Suppiluliuma, I am home and give you the king's answer as he spoke it. Tushratta accepts peace: neither land shall send troops into the other's homeland, envoys shall pass freely, and you shall speak together should Assyria or Babylon trouble either of you. But he will not seal the tablet as you wrote it. He says Isuwa and Carchemish lie at the gates of Harran and Washukanni and are his border, so he will look to them himself; he asks that Ugarit, Lukka and the western coast be your portion, and Qadesh, Mari and Damascus his own. He says he will seal a tablet written so, and gladly. I told him I had no authority from you to seal any exchange of cities, so I bring the tablet back unsealed and have given no word on terms, troops, gold or land. His envoy Tattamaru travels with me to hear your answer. At Mitanni the capital keeps 4 bands of army and no fleet; the court is rich; and Kidin-Adad, envoy of Babylonia, was also at the court.

My lord Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, I, your humble servant Kidin-Adad, have returned from the court of Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, and lay before you what passed. He greeted you as his brother and accepted brotherhood and peace: no troops into each other's homeland, and envoys to pass freely. He sealed your tablet, thanked you for the gift, and I bring the sealed tablet home to you together with the inventory of the gold, unbroken. He desires a steady road for his envoys and word from you of what you see on the Assyrian border, for Assyria has already sent an army against his Terqa. I noted that Mitanni keeps 4 army and no fleet near its capital. I could not pledge your answer to him, being only your messenger, and I await your word.

To my lord, the Great King of Alashiya, from your servant Ili-iddina: I went to the court of Egypt and gave its king your greeting, your wish for peace and trade between your ports, your request that his troops and ships stay out of Enkomi and Tamassos, and your request for a gift of gold, and I laid your tablet of brotherhood before him. He answered that he has heard you, that he is mindful of you, and that he will weigh your tablet and your request for gold with his counselors; his answer will come by his own envoy in due season. He gave no gold and made no promise. I carried his words back to you exactly as he spoke them. In my judgment he is cautious rather than unfriendly, and I think he will not refuse you lightly. I await your command for further service.

My lord Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, I went to the court of Karduniash and gave your greeting and your proposal to the Great King Burna-Buriash, as you bade me. He greets you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses, and he desires quiet roads between brothers. He holds Ekallatum by the fortune of war as he holds Sippar, and counts that settled. As to Susa and Mari he makes no promise today; he will send his own envoy with his word when he has taken counsel, and until then he bids that no rumour trouble your friendship. I answered that I would carry his word to you faithfully and wait upon his counsel at his pleasure. I bring no rumour from his court, and I await your pleasure concerning the wages still owed me.

My lord Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, I have come back from the court of Alashiya as you commanded. Its king greets you, your household, your sons, your chariots and your horses, and says there is no quarrel between your crowns and he wants none; his ships keep to his own coasts. He has sealed your tablet gladly, and it now bears both seals: Arzawa and Alashiya are brothers, neither sends ships or troops against the other's lands, and each warns the other of any king who plans harm to him. He asks only for quiet seas and honest traders, and he sends his brotherhood home to you with me. At his capital I saw no army to speak of and one fleet lying in the harbour. I ask that the wages owed me for this journey be paid in full.

value.speech: O Great King, Suppiluliuma, king of Hatti, my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, greets his brother. May it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots, horses and country. Egypt desires peace and brotherhood with Hatti: Egypt is to hold Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos and Damascus, and Hatti is to hold Ugarit, Carchemish, Isuwa and its own lands. Amurru and Qadesh lie between us, and neither shall take them without the other's word. My lord asks that our envoys pass freely, and that you seal the tablet I bear.

Great King Tushratta, my lord Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt, your brother, sends this word: may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. Egypt and Mitanni have long been friends, and Egypt seeks no land of Mitanni; he asks only for peace and open roads between us, and that each tell the other if a third king moves against either. He asks you to seal the tablet I bring, in which Egypt and Mitanni are named brothers, neither sends troops against the other's lands, and each warns the other when a third king advances.

Hear the words of my lord Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, to his brother Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt. May your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your land prosper. As our fathers were brothers, so let us be; let there be peace between our lands and free passage for our envoys. Gold is as dust in his land and his house is building, so he asks that you send gifts worthy of a brother, and he will answer in kind. I bring a tablet for your seal, to set this brotherhood down in writing.

Paser, say to Napkhururiya, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May all go well with you. Mitanni and Egypt have been friends since our fathers, and I seal your tablet gladly: brothers, no troops against each other's lands, and a warning when a third king advances. I will warn you, and I ask that you warn me. A brother who loves a brother sends gold in plenty, for in your land gold is as dust; let your next envoy bring it, and solid, not gilded wood as was once promised to my father.

Say to Burna-Buriash, Great King of Karduniash, my brother: thus says Napkhururiya, Great King of Egypt. All goes well with me. May all go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. As our fathers were brothers, so we are. I have sealed your tablet: let there be peace and free passage for our envoys. My gifts will follow as my house permits, in measure with what you send. Send your envoys often.

Brother Napkhururiya, may it go well with you, your household, wives, sons, chariots and horses. Suppiluliuma of Hatti sees the tablet and seals it: we are brothers, neither sends troops against the other's land, Hatti holds Ugarit, Carchemish and Isuwa, Egypt holds Gaza, Megiddo, Tyre, Byblos and Damascus. Our envoys shall pass freely in both lands. Carry this home and let Egypt send word before any quarrel arises.

Great King Napkhururiya, your words are heard, and I will carry them to my lord Burna-Buriash exactly as you have spoken them. Your seal is set upon the tablet, and I bear it home as witness that peace and free passage are written between our houses. I will report your promise of gifts, to be given in measure with what Karduniash sends, and I will carry your request that envoys pass often between us.

O Great King, Suppiluliuma, your servant hears and gives thanks. The tablet with your seal shall go home to my lord Napkhururiya, who will rejoice that his brother has sealed the peace between Egypt and Hatti. Envoys shall pass freely in both lands as you have commanded, and Egypt will send word before any quarrel arises. May your name stand high in all lands.
value.commitments: Egypt agrees to exchange envoys and news with Hatti and to send word before any quarrel arises. No gold, troops or Egyptian land promised.

value.speech: Great King Tushratta, your word is heard and I will carry it whole to my lord Napkhururiya. The tablet is sealed: brothers, no troops against each other's lands, each warns the other when a third king advances, and envoys and news shall pass between Egypt and Mitanni. Of gold I can promise nothing; I will carry your asking to my lord, and what he answers he will send by his envoy. May all go well with you, your household and your country.
value.commitments: Sealed the tablet of brotherhood and non-aggression; agreed that Egypt and Mitanni exchange envoys and news and warn each other when a third king advances. No gold, troops or Egyptian land promised.

value.speech: Hear the words of Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, who greets his brother the Great King of Hatti. May your house, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses prosper. The armies of Mitanni sit at Terqa, Taidu and Washukanni, a danger to us both, and my lord proposes an alliance against them: let Hatti take the lands toward Isuwa and Harran, and Assyria Terqa and Taidu, with Washukanni to be settled between our two houses. Let neither of us raise a hand against the other. He asks that you send your terms back with me.

Great King Tushratta, thus my lord Tarhundaradu, Great King of Arzawa, greets his brother of Mitanni and wishes well to your household, your chariots and your country. Hatti sits between our two lands and threatens us both, so he proposes an alliance: neither shall attack the other, Arzawa shall press Hatti from the west while Mitanni presses from the east, and neither shall make peace with Hatti without telling the other. His armies are already moving against Hatti's western lands, and he asks you to tell him what Mitanni intends. I bring a tablet for you to seal before Shamash and Teshub, that the pact may stand between you.

Brother Ashur-uballit, may it go well with you, your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots and your horses. Suppiluliuma of Hatti hears you gladly. Let there be peace between Hatti and Assyria: neither raises a hand against the other, and our envoys pass freely. Your reckoning of the east pleases me. Isuwa, Carchemish and the lands toward Harran I count as Hatti's reach; Terqa and Taidu are Assyria's; Washukanni we settle together when the time comes. I bind myself to no troops or gold today, for my armies are busy in the west and I speak with many courts. Send a tablet in this form, and your envoy to my gate with it, and I will weigh it for sealing. Tell your lord that he who strikes first at Terqa will find Hatti watching, and not unfriendly.

Tulubri, say to Tarhundaradu, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my wives, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May all go well with you. Hatti sits between us and covets what is not hers, and I have seen it myself at Isuwa, where her army met mine. I seal your tablet before Shamash and Teshub: neither of us will attack the other, and neither will make peace with Hatti without telling the other first. I will keep my armies on my eastern and northern roads, and my claim on Isuwa and Carchemish stands. Press Hatti hard in the west, at Lukka, Tuwanuwa and Mira's borders, so that her armies are drawn away from Kanesh and Isuwa. Send me word each season of what Hatti's armies do, and I will do the same. Let our envoys pass freely between our courts.

Great King Tushratta, I will carry your words to my lord Tarhundaradu as you have spoken them, and I wish all good to your household, your wives, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. The tablet is sealed before Shamash and Teshub: neither of us shall attack the other, and neither shall make peace with Hatti without first telling the other. I shall tell my lord to send you word each season of what Hatti's armies do, and that your envoys may pass freely between our courts. May the gods keep the roads open for us both.
value.commitments: On behalf of my lord Tarhundaradu: Arzawa shall not attack Mitanni; Arzawa shall press Hatti in the west; neither king shall make peace with Hatti without first telling the other; each king shall send word each season of what Hatti's armies do; envoys shall pass freely between the courts of Arzawa and Mitanni.

value.speech: Great King Suppiluliuma, I will carry your words to my lord Ashur-uballit as they were spoken, and his household will hear that Hatti hears him gladly. Let there be peace between our houses, neither raising a hand against the other, with our envoys passing freely at both gates. The division my lord proposed, Harran and Isuwa to you and Terqa and Taidu to Assyria, I can answer for. Carchemish my lord did not name, and I cannot bind him to it, so I will bring that question back with the tablet in your form. Washukanni waits upon the time you name.
value.commitments: Non-aggression between Assyria and Hatti, with envoys passing freely; the division my lord proposed: Harran and Isuwa to Hatti, Terqa and Taidu to Assyria, Washukanni to be settled between the two houses when the time comes. No gold, land or troops promised. Carchemish not agreed; referred back to my lord.

value.speech: Hear the word of my lord Ashur-uballit, Great King of Assyria, to you, Tushratta, Great King of Mitanni, his brother. He wishes well to you, your household, sons, chariots, horses and country. Your tablet is sealed and he keeps it. Babylonia's army now stands in Ekallatum, beside your Terqa, and its king keeps no peace with his neighbours; let us be rid of it together. In a season we agree, his army marches from Ashur into Ekallatum, and if your army in Terqa supports that move the garrison cannot hold. Once Ekallatum is his again, his army there will support your army from Terqa into Mari, as you wish. Name the season and send your answer back with me, his envoy, and I bring the tablet for your seal. Shamash is witness.

Ubaru, say to Ashur-uballit, my brother: all goes well with me, my household, my sons, my chariots, my horses and my country. May all go well with you. I have sealed your tablet before Shamash. I name TURN 6. In turn 6 let your army march from Ashur into Ekallatum, and my army in Terqa will support that move. In turn 7, the season after, let your army in Ekallatum support my army from Terqa into Mari, as you promised. Send your orders so that both armies move in the same season, for if one moves alone the support is void and nothing is gained. I keep my army in Terqa until then. Neither of us sends an army into the land of the other. Let us be as brothers against the one who keeps no peace.

Thus my lord Ashur-uballit answers through me, his envoy: all goes well with him, his household, sons, chariots, horses and country, and may all go well with you. Turn 6 is agreed: his army marches from Ashur into Ekallatum, and in turn 7 his army there supports your army from Terqa into Mari, as he has promised. Both armies must move in the same season, and neither enters the other's land. I carry your sealed tablet home to my lord for his seal. Shamash is witness.
value.commitments: On behalf of Ashur-uballit: his army marches from Ashur into Ekallatum in turn 6; once Ekallatum is his again, in turn 7 his army there supports Mitanni's army from Terqa into Mari. Neither sends an army into the other's land. No gold, land or other troops promised.

orders.letter: Ashur-uballit of Assyria wishes well to my brother Burna-Buriash, to your household, your sons, your chariots, your horses and your country. I have heard the words you gave Pirissi and I too desire quiet roads between brothers. Let each king keep what he holds today and let neither send an army against the land of the other: no army of Karduniash into Arbela, Nineveh or Ashur, and none of mine into your provinces. Let Shamash be witness. If you wish to seal a tablet, send your own envoy with your word as you promised, and I will seal it.
orders.mandate: May agree to mutual non-aggression on the present borders, and may say I would seal a tablet to that effect when the Great King of Karduniash sends his own envoy. May not cede any province, promise any gold, or give up my claim to Ekallatum.

value.notes: T3: Gold 104. Babylonia took Susa (their army there) and holds Ekallatum; their ekallatum army tried ->arbela last turn (bounced with my nineveh move). Arbela is EMPTY now. Orders: nineveh->arbela with ashur supporting (2 vs their 1; ties if susa supports ekallatum->arbela), raise army in nineveh (empty after the move; if move bounces no army raised and no pay). Ashur NEVER leaves capital empty. Sent Pirissi (c9) to Babylonia with a non-aggression offer on present borders, no tablet, no gold (gold reserved for the army). Private plan: this peace is a pause only. When c18 returns (T4) read Mitanni's answer on the joint Ekallatum move (Terqa supports ashur->ekallatum, or arbela->ekallatum with ashur support). Need strength 3 if Sippar/Durkurigalzu support Ekallatum's hold. Cash is thin: income 110, 3 armies cost 90, wages up to 36 when c10, c18, c9 are all home. Do not let all three sit at court; dismiss c18 (11) or send people away to defer wages. Do not hire c15/c17 (25/21) yet. Wake T4 to re-plan.
value.summary: Ashur-uballit of Assyria. Start 1700 strength, homeland nineveh/arbela/ashur/ekallatum. T1: attacked Terqa (failed), Babylonia took Ekallatum and destroyed my army there. Bought Susa (walls) T1, Babylonia took it T2 (nippur->susa, ur support). Sealed k4 with Mitanni T2 (no armies into each other's land, no aid to the other's enemy; Mitanni may take Mari/Isuwa/Carchemish/Qadesh, Assyria may take Susa).
